question: Which of the following refers to the newer and younger deposits of the floodplains in the Northern Plains of India, which are renewed almost every year and are therefore very fertile? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Terai
Bhangar
Kankar
Khadar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Khadar

Explanation:
The newer and younger alluvial deposits of the floodplains in the Northern Plains of India are called Khadar. These deposits are renewed almost every year during floods, which makes the soil very fertile and suitable for agriculture. In contrast, Bhangar refers to older alluvial deposits found on higher terraces away from rivers, which are less fertile. Terai is the marshy region at the foothills of the Himalayas, while Kankar are nodules of calcium carbonate found in Bhangar soil. Khadar soil is composed of silt, clay, and sand, and it supports the cultivation of crops like wheat, rice, and sugarcane. The frequent flooding ensures the renewal of nutrients, making it the most productive soil in the region.

☛ How often is Khadar soil renewed? → Annually
☛ What are the calcium carbonate nodules in Bhangar called? → Kankar
☛ Which region is the marshy area at the Himalayan foothills? → Terai
☛ Which crops are suitable for Khadar soil? → Wheat, rice, sugarcane
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन भारत के उत्तरी मैदानों में बाढ़ के मैदानों की नई और युवा जमाओं को संदर्भित करता है, जो लगभग हर साल नवीनीकृत होती हैं और इसलिए बहुत उपजाऊ होती हैं? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 3)

भांगर
कंकर
खादर
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है खादर

Explanation:
भारत के उत्तरी मैदानों में नदियों द्वारा लाई गई नई और युवा जलोढ़ निक्षेपों को खादर कहा जाता है। ये बाढ़ के मैदानों में जमा होते हैं और लगभग हर साल बाढ़ के दौरान नवीनीकृत होते हैं। नवीनीकरण के कारण इनमें उपजाऊ मिट्टी पाई जाती है, जो कृषि के लिए अत्यंत उपयुक्त होती है। इसके विपरीत, भांगर पुरानी जलोढ़ निक्षेपों को कहते हैं जो बाढ़ के मैदानों से ऊपर स्थित होते हैं और कम उपजाऊ होते हैं। तराई हिमालय के पाद-देश में दलदली क्षेत्र है, जबकि कंकर भांगर में पाए जाने वाले कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट के कंकड़ होते हैं। खादर मिट्टी नदियों के आस-पास पाई जाती है और इसमें गाद, मिट्टी और रेत का मिश्रण होता है। यह गेहूं, चावल और गन्ना जैसी फसलों के लिए उपयुक्त है।

question: The Indus River system includes all of the following rivers EXCEPT: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Sutlej
Godavari
Ravi
Jhelum
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Godavari

Explanation:
The Indus River system primarily includes the Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej rivers. These rivers originate in the Himalayas and flow into the Indus in Pakistan. The Godavari river flows in the southwestern part of India and empties into the Bay of Bengal; it is not a part of the Indus system. Godavari is the largest river in peninsular India and is also known as the 'Dakshin Ganga'. The rivers of the Indus system mainly provide water to northern India and Pakistan.

☛ Where does the Godavari river empty? → Bay of Bengal
☛ Which river is called 'Dakshin Ganga'? → Godavari

question: What types of climate and vegetation characterise the Taiga natural region?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Arid deserts with cactus
Cold climate with coniferous forests
Flood-prone swamp areas
Dense tropical vegetation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cold climate with coniferous forests

Explanation:
The Taiga, also known as the boreal forest, is a biome found primarily in Siberia, Scandinavia, Alaska, and Canada. Its climate is characterized by long, cold winters and short, cool summers. Temperatures remain below freezing for most of the year, and precipitation is low. The dominant vegetation consists of coniferous trees such as spruce, pine, fir, and larch, which are adapted to survive harsh cold conditions. Other options are incorrect because arid deserts with cactus are not part of the Taiga, flood-prone swamp areas are found in tropical regions, and dense tropical vegetation is near the equator.

☛ Main tree type in Taiga → Conifers (spruce, pine)
☛ Climate feature of Taiga → Long cold winters and short summers
☛ Continents where Taiga is found → North America, Europe, Asia
☛ Annual rainfall in Taiga → 300-850 mm
question_hi: टैगा प्राकृतिक क्षेत्र की जलवायु और वनस्पति किस प्रकार की होती है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 3)

Explanation:

question: Through which of the following states do the Western Ghats pass? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Punjab
Bihar
Tamil Nadu
Uttar Pradesh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tamil Nadu

Explanation:
The Western Ghats are a mountain range running parallel to the western coast of India. They start from Gujarat and pass through Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu, ending at Kanyakumari. Tamil Nadu covers the southern part of the Western Ghats, where the range loses height. Anamudi and Doddabetta are among the prominent peaks in this range. Punjab, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh are not traversed by the Western Ghats, as they are located in northern or eastern India. The Western Ghats are also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

☛ What is the highest peak of the Western Ghats? → Anamudi (Kerala)
☛ What is the other name of the Western Ghats? → Sahyadri
☛ From which state does the Western Ghats originate? → Gujarat
☛ What is the total length of the Western Ghats? → About 1600 km
☛ Which famous hill station is located in the Western Ghats? → Munnar (Kerala) or Kodaikanal (Tamil Nadu)
question_hi: पश्चिमी घाट निम्नलिखित में से किस राज्य से होकर गुजरते हैं? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 1)

question: Why is canal irrigation more suitable in the northern plains of India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: The rivers flow only during monsoon season.
The area suffers from very low annual rainfall.
The surface is uneven and covered with hills.
The flat land and perennial rivers support canal networks
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The flat land and perennial rivers support canal networks

Explanation:
In the northern plains of India, rivers are perennial, fed by melting Himalayan snow and monsoon rains. The terrain is flat, making canal construction and water distribution easy. Other options are incorrect: rivers do not flow only during monsoon; the area has moderate to high rainfall (60-200 cm); and the surface is flat, not uneven.

☛ Geographical requirement for canal irrigation → Flat land and availability of water source.

☛ Advantage of canal irrigation → Reduces dependence on rainfall and provides regular water supply.

question: Chilika Lake and Pulicat Lake are located in which of the following?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: West Coast of India
Malabar Coast
Konkan Coast
East Coast of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is East Coast of India

Explanation:
Chilika Lake is located in Odisha, while Pulicat Lake lies on the border of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. Both are situated on the East Coast of India. Chilika is the largest brackish water lake in India and is also a designated wetland of international importance. Pulicat is the second largest brackish water lake in India. The East Coast features several lagoons and lakes, with Chilika and Pulicat being prominent examples. These lakes are separated from the Bay of Bengal by sandbars and are important ecosystems supporting diverse flora and fauna.

☛ Major wildlife sanctuary on Chilika Lake? → Chilika Bird Sanctuary, famous for migratory birds

☛ Which river does not connect to Chilika Lake? → Daya River
☛ Name lakes located on East Coast of India? → Chilika Lake, Pulicat Lake, Kolleru Lake

question: Colonial policies led to the commercialisation of agriculture. Which of the following crops was encouraged for export during British rule? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Maize
Indigo
Barley
Pulses
solution:

Explanation:
During British rule, agriculture was commercialised to export raw materials from India. Indigo cultivation was particularly encouraged because it was used as a dye in the European textile industry. question: In the first phase of the Green Revolution (approximately mid 1960s upto mid 1970s), the use of HYV seeds was restricted to the more affluent states such as _________.  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Rajasthan, Gujarat and Kerala
Bihar, Odisha and West Bengal
Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Assam
Punjab, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Punjab, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu

Explanation:
In the first phase of the Green Revolution (mid-1960s to mid-1970s), the use of HYV seeds (High Yielding Variety) was primarily restricted to affluent states like Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu. These states had better irrigation facilities and financially capable farmers who could afford the expensive seeds. HYV seeds required higher inputs of fertilizers and pesticides, which these states could sustain. This phase led to a dramatic increase in wheat and rice production, making India self-sufficient in food grains. The revolution later spread to other states in subsequent phases.

question: Which theory suggests that planets were formed out of a cloud of material surrounding a young Sun? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Collision Theory
Binary Star Hypothesis
Nebular Hypothesis
Big Bang Theory
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nebular Hypothesis

Explanation:
The Nebular Hypothesis suggests that the Solar System formed from a large cloud of gas and dust (nebula) that collapsed under gravity, spinning and flattening into a disk. The Sun formed at the center, and planets formed from the remaining material. This theory was proposed by Immanuel Kant and Pierre-Simon Laplace in the 18th century. The Collision Theory and Binary Star Hypothesis are different concepts. The Big Bang Theory explains the origin of the universe, not the Solar System.

☛ Collision Theory explains planet formation by? → Collision and accretion
question_hi: कौन सा सिद्धांत बताता है कि ग्रह एक युवा सूर्य के चारों ओर सामग्री के बादल से बने थे? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 2)

निहारिका परिकल्पना (Nebular Hypothesis) के अनुसार, सौरमंडल का निर्माण एक विशाल गैस और धूल के बादल (निहारिका) से हुआ। यह बादल धीरे-धीरे सिकुड़ा और घूमने लगा, जिससे केंद्र में सूर्य का निर्माण हुआ। बाकी सामग्री से ग्रहों का निर्माण हुआ। यह सिद्धांत 18वीं शताब्दी में इमैनुएल कांट और पियरे-साइमन लाप्लास ने प्रस्तावित किया था। संघट्टन सिद्धांत (Collision Theory) और बाइनरी स्टार हाइपोथीसिस (Binary Star Hypothesis) अलग-अलग अवधारणाएँ हैं। बिग बैंग सिद्धांत ब्रह्मांड की उत्पत्ति से संबंधित है।

question: Sharing borders with the states of Kerala and Karnataka, Mudumalai National Park of Tamil Nadu is a part of which biosphere reserve of India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve
Kangchendzonga Biosphere Reserve
Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve
Nokrek Biosphere Reserve
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve

Explanation:
Mudumalai National Park is located in the Nilgiri district of Tamil Nadu and shares its borders with Kerala and Karnataka. It is an integral part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, which stretches across the Nilgiri hills of the Western Ghats. Established in 1986, it is India's first biosphere reserve. Besides Mudumalai, it includes Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary (Kerala), Bandipur National Park (Karnataka), and Nagarhole National Park (Karnataka). This area is renowned for wildlife such as tigers, elephants, and leopards and is recognized by UNESCO.

question: The Himalayan Mountain ranges stretch in a west-east direction from the Indus River to which major Indian river?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Godavari
Brahmaputra
Ganga
Yamuna
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Brahmaputra

Explanation:
The Himalayan mountain ranges stretch approximately 2,400 km from the Indus River in the west to the Brahmaputra River in the east. The Himalayas are divided into three parallel ranges: the Himadri (Greater Himalayas), Himachal (Middle Himalayas), and Shivaliks (Outer Himalayas). They were formed by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates. The Brahmaputra River originates in Tibet as the Tsangpo and enters India as the Dihang. The Himalayas form India's northern boundary and are the source of many major rivers in Asia, including the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra.

question: Which crop is primarily associated with plantation agriculture in Kerala?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 3)

question: Why is air transport less popular for freight movement in India?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: It is widely available in rural and remote villages.
It requires minimal infrastructure for operation.
It is expensive and ideal only for light, high-value goods.
It is slower and less efficient than water transport
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It is expensive and ideal only for light, high-value goods.

Explanation:
Air transport is less popular for freight movement in India because it is significantly expensive compared to other modes. High costs of aviation fuel, aircraft maintenance, and airport charges make it unaffordable for bulk or low-value goods. Therefore, air freight is suitable only for light, high-value items such as electronics, pharmaceuticals, and perishables, where time savings justify the expense. For heavy or low-value goods, road and rail transport offer cheaper alternatives. Additionally, air transport has limited capacity and can be affected by weather conditions. India's air cargo infrastructure is also relatively underdeveloped, especially in smaller cities. Hence, due to high cost and limited suitability, air transport remains less popular for freight movement.

Explanation:
भारत में माल ढुलाई के लिए हवाई परिवहन कम लोकप्रिय है क्योंकि यह अन्य साधनों की तुलना में काफी महंगा है। हवाई ईंधन, विमान रखरखाव और हवाईअड्डा शुल्क अधिक होते हैं, जिससे लागत बढ़ जाती है। इसलिए, हवाई परिवहन केवल हल्के, उच्च-मूल्य वाले सामानों जैसे इलेक्ट्रॉनिक्स, फार्मास्यूटिकल्स और नाशवान वस्तुओं के लिए उपयुक्त है, जहां समय की बचत लागत को उचित ठहराती है। भारी या कम मूल्य के सामान के लिए सड़क और रेलवे अधिक किफायती हैं। इसके अलावा, हवाई परिवहन की क्षमता सीमित होती है और यह मौसम से प्रभावित हो सकता है। भारत में हवाई कार्गो बुनियादी ढांचा भी अपेक्षाकृत कम विकसित है, खासकर छोटे शहरों में। इस प्रकार, उच्च लागत और सीमित उपयुक्तता के कारण हवाई परिवहन माल ढुलाई के लिए कम लोकप्रिय है।

question: Which type of weathering is primarily involved in the enrichment of bauxite and other ores? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Mechanical weathering
Glacial weathering
Biological weathering
Chemical weathering
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chemical weathering

Explanation:
The enrichment of bauxite and other ores primarily involves chemical weathering. In this process, minerals in rocks react with water, oxygen, and carbon dioxide, leading to their decomposition. In tropical regions, high temperature and rainfall accelerate chemical weathering, removing silica and other soluble elements, while concentrating iron and aluminum oxides. This results in the formation of bauxite from aluminum-rich rocks. Chemical weathering is thus crucial for the formation of residual deposits like bauxite and laterite ores.

question: What is the general slope of the Deccan Plateau? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: North to South
West to East
South to North
East to West
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is West to East

Explanation:
The general slope of the Deccan Plateau is from West to East. This is primarily because the Western Ghats are higher than the Eastern Ghats. Rivers like Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri originate from the Western Ghats and flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal, clearly demonstrating this slope. The Deccan Plateau is a large plateau in peninsular India, with an ancient geological structure. The elevation difference between the Western and Eastern Ghats determines the drainage pattern, making the plateau tilt from west to east. This slope influences the river systems and agricultural patterns in the region.

question_hi: दक्कन के पठार की सामान्य ढलान क्या है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 2)

पूर्व से पश्चिम
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है पश्चिम से पूर्व

Explanation:
दक्कन के पठार की सामान्य ढलान पश्चिम से पूर्व की ओर है। इसका प्रमुख कारण यह है कि पश्चिमी घाट पूर्वी घाट की तुलना में ऊँचे हैं। नदियाँ जैसे गोदावरी, कृष्णा, और कावेरी पश्चिमी घाट से निकलकर पूर्वी तट की ओर बहती हैं, जो इस ढलान को प्रदर्शित करती हैं। दक्कन का पठार प्रायद्वीपीय भारत का एक विशाल भाग है और इसकी भूगर्भीय संरचना प्राचीन है। यह ढलान नदी अपवाह प्रणाली को प्रभावित करती है। पश्चिमी घाट और पूर्वी घाट के बीच ऊँचाई का अंतर इस ढलान का मुख्य कारण है।
